definitions.explanation: Tailored trousers with a crease, typically worn as part of business or smart-casual attire. Distinguished from jeans or casual pants by their neat, pressed appearance.

examples.japanese: スラックス⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦アイロン→アイロン：05071_airon⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かけた→かける：00854_kakeru⟧。
⟦{黒|くろ}い→黒い：00588_kuroi⟧スラックス⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}いたい→買う：00489_kau⟧。
examples.english: I want to buy black slacks.

examples.japanese: ⟦ジーンズ→ジーンズ：00123_jiinzu⟧⟦ではなく→ではなく：09578_dehanaku⟧スラックス⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{履|は}いて→履く：00700_haku⟧⟦{面接|めんせつ}→面接：01100_mensetsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}った→行く：00119_iku⟧⟦{方|ほう}→方：01139_hou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧。
examples.english: You should wear slacks rather than jeans to the interview.

notes:
スラックス comes from English "slacks." In Japanese, it specifically refers to tailored, pressed trousers suitable for business or formal settings.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- スラックス⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{履|は}く→履く：00700_haku⟧ — to wear slacks
- スラックス⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦アイロン→アイロン：05071_airon⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かける→かける：00854_kakeru⟧ — to iron slacks
- スラックス⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{折|お}り{目|め} — crease in slacks

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦ズボン→ズボン：01072_zubon⟧ — trousers/pants (general term, from French "jupon")
- ⟦パンツ→パンツ：01374_pantsu⟧ — pants (modern general term; also means underwear)
- チノパン — chinos

スラックス is always plural in form (following English), but Japanese treats it as a regular singular noun. Counted with {本|ほん} (⟦{一本|いっぽん}→一本：08888_ippon⟧, {二本|にほん}...).
